scope: Formal statewide New Jersey moving-water corridor inventory and strict route-package review

inventory.routeCandidateDisposition: Every corridor family is classified as route_candidate, blocked, or screened_out in docs/operations/new-jersey-statewide-inventory.json; every route_candidate family has one or more registered route slugs; every prioritized USGS lead has an explicit covered-by-catalog-family or blocked-pending-route-package disposition in the generated inventory.

latestBlockedFamilyReviews.finding: American Whitewater identifies a 3.9-mile Class II–IV reach with short-duration storm flow, strainers, low bridges, and no developed or standard put-ins/take-outs. NJDEP’s access list is an angling baseline rather than paddle-launch authorization; USGS provides same-creek monitoring context.

NJDEP identifies School Street and Van Syckel’s Corner Road fishing-access settings, and American Whitewater lists an Upper Spruce Run Class II reach with USGS gauge context. No current lawful canoe/kayak endpoint pair independent of fishing access was established; the downstream reservoir transition requires separate controls.

American Whitewater identifies a Class III–IV Upper Creek Road-to-Covered Bridge reach, but the available flow listing is stale and the NJDEP access listing is a fishing/roadside setting rather than a verified paddle launch. A current two-endpoint package with route-specific hazard and access authorization did not clear review.

USGS identifies Raccoon Creek at Wrights Mill as a current monitored stream and NJDEP identifies Raccoon Creek WMA and fishing-access holdings, but the reviewed official sources do not establish two lawful paddle endpoints or route-specific safety and landing controls. County canoe/kayak facilities found in this pass are on Wilson Lake/Scotland Run, not the moving Raccoon Creek channel.

Current NJDEP access listings and USGS 01379845 telemetry are useful reconnaissance evidence, but they do not establish independent paddle launch rights or a single bounded route. The Boonton Gorge reach remains a separate expert Class IV–V and legal/access question.

NJDEP access listings and USGS 01387500 telemetry identify a real New Jersey corridor, but the reviewed sources do not establish independent canoe/kayak launch rights or a continuous New Jersey endpoint pair. The Tuxedo-to-Suffern whitewater description does not supply New Jersey-specific authorization.
